_comment: Every slot passes through lib/media.ts, which withholds an image unless FIVE things are true at once: a non-empty path, permission.granted === true, publish !== false, tier !== 'C', and alt text in at least one locale. A slot missing any one of them resolves to null and the component renders its designed placeholder instead.
_comment_permission: permission.granted is a SEPARATE field from path on purpose. Having the file and having the right to publish it are two different things, and the first is never evidence of the second. scripts/check-publish-gate.mjs fails the build (exit 1) on any slot that has a path without a recorded permission, so the two are always set together.
_comment_alt: Alt text is part of the gate rather than a nicety: an image that cannot be described has not been understood well enough to publish. Intake form section 5 also requires that people in a photo be named and that event photos carry dates, neither portrait here contains anyone but the subject.

slots._comment_cutout: THE PATH IS A SUPPLIED CUT-OUT AND IS NOT DERIVED OR PROCESSED BY THIS REPO. The client supplied sanae-rakik-portrait-supplied-cutout.png with the background already removed, and asked explicitly that no edge treatment of any kind be applied to it. It is therefore copied in BYTE FOR BYTE (verified with cmp) and nothing in the build touches it. scripts/build-portrait-cutout.mjs still exists and still targets the original JPEG, but its output is NO LONGER WHAT THE SITE RENDERS; do not re-point this path at it without asking, that would silently reinstate the edge processing the client declined. KNOWN AND ACCEPTED: 601,698 of the transparent pixels in this file still carry white in their colour channels. That is invisible at full size, but next/image resizes non-premultiplied, so a downscale averages that white into the silhouette and can re-create a faint pale rim at larger widths (measured: 0 bright edge pixels at w=384, 1 at w=544, 60 at w=1080, 182 at w=1200). The client chose the file as supplied over having this corrected. If a pale edge is ever reported on a high-DPI screen, this is the cause and the fix is a colour-bleed pass that fills transparent pixels with their neighbours' colour and never touches the alpha channel or the silhouette.

slots._comment: Intake form section 5 requires a professional horizontal image at no less than 1920px for a full-bleed backdrop. Neither supplied file reaches that width (1206px), and upscaling would produce exactly the 'صور غير احترافية أو منخفضة الجودة' the same section forbids. The slot stays empty and the hero renders its built backdrop, which is a permanent floor rather than a placeholder awaiting deletion.

organisationId must match a row id in data/positions.json for getOrganisationLogo() to find it. A third-party logo needs the organisation's own permission, not the subject's; this was closed on that basis and was OPENED BY EXPLICIT INSTRUCTION FROM THE SITE OWNER on 2026-09-18, who directed that this mark be used. See _comment_permission.
slots._comment_alt: Written for the case where the mark appears WITHOUT the organisation named beside it. In the hero it is rendered decorative (alt="") because the full legal name is already set as text directly above it, and repeating it would make a screen reader announce the same name twice.
slots._comment_permission: OPENED ON THE SITE OWNER'S INSTRUCTION, AND THE RECORD SAYS SO RATHER THAN IMPLYING MORE. `grantedBy` is the site owner, who on 2026-09-18 supplied this file and directed that it be published here. That is a real authorisation from the person who owns this site and holds the IBC relationship, and it is what this record claims - nothing wider. IBC's own countersigned confirmation is a separate document and is still not on file, so the org-logos row in data/deliverables.json stays permissionRecorded:false and the open item stays open until it is. docs/content-gaps.md:207-212 explains why the council's own agreement is still worth obtaining: it is the thing that protects the relationship if the mark's use is ever questioned.

slots._comment_dimensions: The supplied file is a 1920x1080 frame with the lockup centred in it, so most of its area is empty white. These are the dimensions of the ARTWORK once trimmed to its bounding box, which is what next/image needs to lay the mark out at its true aspect ratio; a 16:9 box would reserve a band of empty space around it. If the trimmed file is replaced, re-measure these.

_comment_never: Nothing is added here that the subject does not hold the rights to. Event and conference photography is usually the photographer's copyright regardless of who appears in it, so a file arriving by message is not by itself a permission.
